standard_prerequisites.name: Conditions, stabilisation, the limit colouring and progressiveness
standard_prerequisites.statement: The section works with conditions, each a triple of a colouring constrained by a computable bounding function, a finite stem and an infinite reservoir computing a fixed set D, with the two defining properties (a) and (b) of a condition; a reservoir stabilises an interval when the images of its finite sets land in fixed finite sets of short tuples, and to such a reservoir the section attaches a limit colouring whose values are the unions of those finite sets; a function into finite sets of natural numbers is progressive when every nonempty value has least element at least the least element of its argument. The author's own definitions are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the core combinatorial step of the diagonalisation: it says exactly when a finite block of reservoir elements may be appended to the stem without destroying property (b), and the extensibility lemma later in the section combines it with two other lemmas of the same section.

core_obligations: Fix an arbitrary finite subset of the union of the stem, the block and the reservoir, of admissible size, and split the analysis into three cases according to whether it meets the stem, meets the block, or meets neither (source line 1169).

First case, the set meets the stem: the two defining properties of the original condition give that the image of the set meets the union of the stem with the old reservoir inside the set itself, and since the new stem is contained in the union of the stem with the old reservoir, the same holds with the block added (source line 1171).

Second case, the set meets the block but not the stem: write the set as the disjoint union of its part inside the block and its part inside the reservoir, use that the block is free for the limit colouring to see that the value of the limit colouring at the first part meets the block inside that part, use the definition of the limit colouring to place the image of the whole set inside that value, and conclude that the image meets the block inside the set; property (b) for the stem part comes from the original condition (source line 1172).

Third case, the set meets neither the stem nor the block, so it lies inside the reservoir: since the least element of the reservoir is larger than every element of the stem and of the block, progressiveness of the colouring makes the image of the set disjoint from the new stem altogether (source line 1173).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix a finite set of admissible size and split into the three cases.
Case 1: the set meets the stem, so the original properties settle both parts.
Case 2: the set meets the block, dismembered into a block part and a reservoir part using freeness for the limit colouring.
Case 3: the set lies in the reservoir, and progressiveness keeps the image off the new stem.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2412.11598v3 的 Lemma lem:fs-preserving-b（源 1162-1167 行，证明 1168-1175 行）：设 (f,σ,X) 是 condition，Y 稳定 [0,k] 且 g_{k,Y} 为极限着色，若 ρ ⊆ X↾_k 是有限的 g_{k,Y}-free 集，则 (f, σ∪ρ, Y) 满足性质 (b)。关键操作不是例行核验：证明必须按 s 与 σ、ρ、Y 三部分的相交情况分三类。Case 1 用原 condition 的 (a)(b) 直接把 f(s)∩(σ∪ρ) 收进 s（1171 行）；Case 2 是真正的核心——要把 s 拆成 t=s∩ρ 与 u=s∩Y，用 ρ 对极限着色的 free 性得到 g_{k,Y}(t)∩ρ ⊆ t，再用 g_{k,Y}(t) 的定义（含 I_{t,n}）把 f(s)=f(t,u) 放进 I_{t,|u|} ⊆ g_{k,Y}(t)，从而 f(s)∩ρ ⊆ t（1172 行）；Case 3 要求用 min Y > max(σ∪ρ) 与 f 的 progressive 性说明 f(s) 与 σ∪ρ 根本不相交（1173 行）。难点在于 Case 2 要把「极限着色 free」与「稳定化定义中的有限集 I_{t,n}」两层结构对齐；原文位置在证明的 1169、1171、1172、1173 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:fs-preserving-b at source lines 1162-1167 together with its proof at source lines 1168-1175, a straight adjacent pairing in the pinned file. The pinned file is a concatenation of the authors' main and macro files; it is the article's fixed version arXiv:2412.11598v3 under CC BY 4.0.

This source ships no separate preamble file, so the retained preamble is sliced mechanically from the pinned file by the lane and is shared, byte for byte, with the other cards of this source; it carries the authors' full macro block, including the restriction symbol that the retained statement uses.

Three context spans carry the material the retained statement and proof rely on: the convention at line 1119 fixing the bounded-constrained colouring, the definition at line 1152 of the bounding function formed from the Catalan numbers, and the author's definition at lines 1154-1156 of the limit colouring attached to a stabilising reservoir. They are context, not counted units, and none overlaps the counted interval. The definition of a progressive function that the third case uses is recorded in the standard prerequisites instead of being carried as a span: that definition sits at line 1017, and any retained interval reaching back that far would also contain the still-open proof environment at line 1091 of a proposition that another lane counts, which the gate's interval self-check rightly refuses.

The retained statement and proof contain no reference to another labelled result of the article and no citation, so this card carries no navigation pointer and no bibliography entry. In particular the two neighbouring lemmas of the same section are not named inside this span even though the section later combines all three.
